source.version: Journal version of record: Research in Engineering Design (2026) 37:34, published online 31 August 2026 (received 3 April 2026, revised 30 June 2026, accepted 13 July 2026), labeled 'Review Article' in the header although it reports an experiment
source.title_on_document: Human or model? A four-factor experimental study of design experience and image-generation alignment strategies in industrial product ideation

supplement.holds: No supplementary material or online appendix is mentioned. Data availability statement (p. 17): 'No datasets were generated or analysed during the current study.'

paper_design_summary: Sixty participants, grouped by a pre-test into 3 design-experience levels x 2 AIGC-proficiency levels (10 per cell, not randomized), each completed four 10-minute motorcycle concept-design tasks in the lab: Midjourney V6 or ChatGPT-4o image generation crossed with concrete or abstract prompts (within-person, order set by a 4x4 balanced Latin square). Every condition used generative AI; there is no no-AI condition. Two senior product-design experts rated the one representative image each participant selected per condition for creative quality and novelty and coded its attributes for an image-level 'creative diversity' score; participants also self-reported perceived usefulness.

studies.label: Motorcycle concept-design lab experiment (3 EXP x 2 ATP x 2 IGAS x 2 PT mixed design)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Within person: all four combinations of image-generation system (Midjourney V6 vs ChatGPT-4o image generation) and prompt type (concrete vs abstract); task order set by a balanced Latin square. Between-person factors (design experience, AIGC tool proficiency) were classified from a pre-test questionnaire, not assigned.
assignment.quote: To control for order effects, task sequences were assigned using a 4 × 4 balanced Latin square design.
assignment.locator: p. 7, Sect. 3.3 Procedure (first line); design framework p. 6, Sect. 3.2.2; between-subjects grouping p. 5, Sect. 3.1

participants.exclusions: None reported. 60 recruited; ANOVA error df of 54 (Tables 4-6) is consistent with all 60 analyzed. Each participant is in all four within-person conditions; arm n of 60 is the same 60 people.
participants.who: Participants from the authors' affiliated universities (Acknowledgements, p. 17), grouped into no design experience (non-design majors, <1 year training), basic (1-3 years systematic design training), advanced (>3 years professional design education or practice, led at least two projects), crossed with low/high AIGC tool proficiency; 10 per cell. Population code is an inference: the paper does not state that all participants were students.
participants.country: not_stated (all author affiliations are in China)
participants.quote: Considering operational feasibility and group balance, 60 participants were ultimately recruited, ensuring n = 10 per experimental cell to satisfy statistical power requirements.
participants.locator: p. 5, Sect. 3.1 Participants; 'The 60 participants were evenly distributed across six experimental groups, with 10 individuals per group' p. 5

ai_tool.name_model: Midjourney V6 (default resolution, random seeds, style ~750) and ChatGPT-4o image generation (new chat window per task); both accessed March 2025
ai_tool.how_used: Participants typed prompts of the assigned type (concrete: form, material, colour, structure; abstract: metaphorical, emotional, atmospheric) into the assigned system, generated as many motorcycle concepts as possible in 10 minutes, then selected one image as the representative output for that condition. Researchers checked prompts for compliance.

task.description: Generate as many innovative motorcycle design concepts as possible with the assigned image-generation system and prompt type; submit one representative image per condition (four images per participant).
task.duration: 10 minutes per condition, four conditions, ~5-minute rest between tasks; ~5-minute training video beforehand; ~5-minute interview afterwards

outcomes.name: Creative quality (expert rating)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two senior product-design experts (>7 years industry and teaching), blind to condition, rated five dimensions (functional completeness, aesthetic/formal quality, technical feasibility, user orientation, overall completeness) on 1-5 scales; final score = mean of the two experts. Cronbach alpha 0.847; ICC(3,2)=0.703, 95% CI [0.664, 0.737] (p. 9). Analysed with four-factor mixed repeated-measures ANOVA, Holm-Bonferroni post hoc.

outcomes.name: Image-level attribute 'creative diversity' score
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Two experts coded each submitted image on four attributes (form/structure, material and surface, conceptual style, ergonomics; Table 1 categories); score = equal-weighted average of four attribute-level variety measures V1-V4, range 0 to 1. Variety within ONE image, not similarity across people's outputs, so coded 'other' rather than 'diversity'. The formula itself is not printed in the PDF (p. 8). Analysed with Aligned Rank Transform ANOVA because of non-normality; Tukey-adjusted ART contrasts.

eligibility.reason: All participants used generative AI in every condition; the AI contrast is within person (Midjourney V6 vs ChatGPT-4o image generation, crossed with prompt type), an ai_design comparison. Order was counterbalanced with a 4x4 balanced Latin square, but the paper never says participants were randomly allocated to sequences, and the codebook admits within-person designs only when order is randomized. Between-subjects factors were classified from a pre-test, not assigned. 60 people analyzed (>= 50). Expert-rated quality and novelty are scored on the output.

one_line_finding: With 60 participants each using both tools, expert-rated quality was higher for Midjourney V6 than ChatGPT-4o images (3.58 vs 3.11; diff 0.469, SE 0.107, p < 0.001), as was novelty (3.12 vs 2.68; diff 0.444, p = 0.003) (p. 9 Table 3; p. 12 Table 5; p. 14 Table 6).
open_questions: Does a balanced Latin square without stated random allocation to sequences meet criterion 1 for within-person designs?
Which system is the 'treatment' arm in the IGAS ai_design contrast? Neither is a default configuration; I set Midjourney V6 as treatment to match the paper's reported direction (IGAS0 > IGAS1).
The scored output is one participant-selected AI-generated image per condition; does selection among AI images count as the participant's own output for criterion 3?
notes: No condition without AI, so no ai_vs_bau contrast exists. The paper's 'creative diversity' is attribute variety within a single image (p. 8: 'the unit of classification and analysis was the individual submitted image, rather than a set of generated images or an image pool'), so it does not answer across_people. The diversity formula is referenced but not printed (p. 8). Text and Table 3 disagree on some SDs and one mean (quality PT0 3.46 in text vs 3.47 in Table 3; usefulness SDs). Table 3 reports marginal means/SDs per factor level only; per-condition cell means appear only in Fig. 5 for quality. Header labels the article 'Review Article' though it is an experiment. Design experience (EXP) effects were not significant for quality, novelty, or diversity (Tables 5-7).
